messages:
maria: Heads up — saw a recurring 99th pct latency spike during long-context (24k-32k) chat workloads. It correlates with heavy KV pager activity + eviction churn.

jon: same. Repro on staging when kernel selection picks the AVX2 fused kernel for attention (int8 path). Not sure why that ties into paging but timeline matches. :thinking:

lee: can you paste the perf output? wondering if reclaim threads are being starved by the inference worker.

maria: here's the quick snippet from the trace (reduced):

```
[2026-03-15T14:23:12Z] req=chat-8242 enter serve
  kv: miss, allocate page, evict candidate set size=64
  evicter: FIFO chosen, reinsert=false
  cpu: inference kernel int8_gemm (AVX2) pinned
  reclaim: background sweep queued, latency=120ms
  req stalled waiting for pager lock
  latency total: 420ms (baseline ~60ms)
```

jon: interesting — FIFO chosen repeatedly for hot prefixes. On FIFO we expected reinserts on reuse but config has reinserts disabled for that slot. Could be correctness mismatch between eviction policy and the reinsert heuristic.

lee: I profiled kernel scheduling: inference threads monopolize the NIC and memory controller during the kernel, which delays the evicter's lock acquisition. When the kernel is long (int8 path + long seq), eviction/paging stacks up and subsequent requests block on pager lock.

maria: also saw fragmentation increase over a long session (many small KV entries). Free list walking gets longer and evicter cost grows O(n).

jon: hypothesis: batching heuristics align multiple long-context requests into one batch, which increases peak KV working set; combined with AVX2 kernel latency, it causes the evicter to flip to FIFO (because hotness counters hit window threshold) and then reinserts are suppressed -> wrong eviction ordering and stalls.

lee: what about correctness? Any evidence of data corruption or just latency?

maria: no corruption — but some requests served stale KV entries when reuse window was short. There's a race where a reinsert may be lost if evicter checkpoint preempts reinsert writer. I think we have an atomicity bug in reinsert path under high concurrency.

perf-bot: Deployed commit e7d3a4 to staging (kv/evict: increase evicter lock fairness) — trace id: <https://perf.internal/trace/2691>

jon: tested e7d3a4 — 99th dropped ~22% but still have spikes at specific tails. I ran a micro-repro that toggles kernel selection: forcing float32 kernels (slower per-token but shorter stalls) removed the heavy pager waits.

lee: that suggests the kernel's memory-bandwidth behavior is the amplifier, not the eviction algo alone. Can we try two experiments in staging: 1) enable reinsert-on-serve for FIFO, 2) lower batching window from 15ms to 6ms for long-context route.

maria: did 1) yesterday: enabling reinserts reduced eviction churn but increased fragmentation a bit and increased memory by ~8%. 2) lowering batching window helped — 99th improved another ~18% but throughput dropped ~6%.

jon: notes from profiler: when reinserts are enabled, we saw a small race condition manifest in logs: "reinsert lost: evicter checkpointed entry before write-back". I added an assert and hit it once. Sounds like we need an atomic handoff or a compare-exchange on entry state.

lee: proposed fix: introduce a lightweight per-slot CAS for reinsert operations; if CAS fails, retry fast without taking global evicter lock. Also throttle kernel selection for long-context batches to prefer kernels with lower memory stall characteristics (even if slightly slower FLOPS).

maria: agrees. I'll put up a draft CL with CAS and a config flag to bias kernel selection for routes with avg seq > 8k.

jon: add a metric: evicter_cas_retries and evicter_lock_wait_ms per-route. Want to correlate with 99th.

perf-bot: Experiment created: exp/kv-reinsert-cas-2026-03-15 — rollout 10% in staging.

maria: initial staging 10% looks promising: 99th down ~35% on the affected route, evicter_lock_wait_ms median dropped from 42ms -> 9ms. CAS retries are low (~0.8 per successful reinsert).

lee: good. follow-ups: investigate free-list scan cost (maybe maintain small per-shard free caches), and add a background compaction job for long-lived sessions to reduce fragmentation.

jon: also update docs for kernel_profiles: add "memory_stall_score" so router can bias kernel selection at request-time.

maria: I'll open the three PRs: CAS patch, batching-window knob per-route, kernel-profile metric. Planning to ramp exp to 50% tomorrow if 10% stays stable.

lee: thanks — please drop the repro script in the thread so QE can run load tests.

maria: will do. linking it shortly.
